blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Paleolithic humans were nomadic hunter-gatherers with no knowledge of agriculture, animal rearing, or pottery.
Early humans in India used hard rocks called quartzite for making crude tools, earning them the name 'Quartzite Men'.
The Paleolithic Age is divided into Lower, Middle, and Upper Paleolithic based on tool technology and climatic changes.
Traces of ash found in Kurnool caves (Andhra Pradesh) indicate the discovery and use of fire during this period.
Bhimbetka rock shelters in Madhya Pradesh contain famous pre-historic paintings depicting hunting scenes and daily life.

blocks.content: The Paleolithic Age is the longest phase of human history. It extended from about 2 million years ago to around 10,000 BC.

Humans during this period lived a very simple and hard life. They depended completely on nature for survival. - They were hunters and gatherers. - They hunted wild animals and gathered fruits, roots, and berries. - There was no knowledge of agriculture or animal domestication. - People lived in caves and rock shelters. - There was no permanent settlement.
Paleolithic humans were nomadic hunter-gatherers who relied on crude quartzite stone tools for their survival.

items: Tools were made of rough and unpolished stone.
Important tools included hand axes, cleavers, and choppers.
These tools were used for cutting meat, hunting animals, and digging roots.

blocks.content: One of the most important achievements of Paleolithic humans was the discovery of fire. Fire was used for: - Cooking food - Protection from wild animals - Providing warmth in cold climates

blocks.content: Paleolithic humans expressed themselves through cave paintings. - These paintings mainly depict hunting scenes, animals, and daily life. - The most famous site of Paleolithic cave paintings in India is Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh.

items: Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for Paleolithic rock art and cave paintings.
Kurnool Caves (Andhra Pradesh) provide the earliest direct archaeological evidence of fire usage in India.
Paleolithic humans in Indian history are commonly referred to as 'Quartzite Men' due to their exclusive choice of quartzite rock for crafting tools.
